Abstract:

Health is a fundamental component of human well-being and development. In this context, Cardiometabolic Diseases (CMD) study is important, which constitutes a major public health concern in low and middle-income countries, like India. CMDs encompass hypertension, heart disease, and diabetes, resulting in significant morbidity, premature mortality, disability, productivity loss, and rising healthcare expenditure. Epidemiological transition, population ageing, urbanisation, and sedentary lifestyles have accelerated the burden of CMDs in India. Despite the growing burden of CMDs, evidence integrating spatiotemporal disease patterns, healthcare utilisation, socio-economic consequences, and future burden in a comprehensive study remains limited. To study this, the National Sample Survey and Sample Registration System databases of India will be used through appropriate spatial and statistical techniques. The objective of the study are: &nbspfirst, to examine the spatiotemporal patterns of CMD burden second, to assess and predict socioeconomic inequalities in healthcare utilisation &nbspthird, to evaluate the financial burden of cardiometabolic care on households' out-of-pocket expenditure and distress financing, also to estimate premature mortality and productivity losses and forth, to quantify and project the future trajectory of cardiometabolic disease burden across diverse demographic groups and geographic regions in India. The findings will highlight vulnerable populations, regions, socio-economic consequences of CMDs, and healthcare needs. It will strengthen evidence-based healthcare planning, policies for the prevention and control of CMDs, reduce regional syndemic vulnerabilities, and improve financial risk protection in India.
